root_idea.summary: A root of spreading and dispersing outward from a single thing, especially through visible extension or branching.
root_idea.development: This orientation appears in the kindling and spreading of fire, the visible spread of gray hair, the scattering of people or objects, and dispersed flows; several derived nouns extend it to flames, fire-bearing implements, and related occupations.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The sole Quran-attested group is displayed under the normalized Form VIII perfect citation form.

senses.definition: To flare or spread visibly; in the Quranic image, grayness spread conspicuously over the head.
senses.usage_conditions: Used in the construction وَاشْتَعَلَ الرَّأْسُ شَيْبًا, where the spread and brightness of gray hair are compared with a blaze. This is a figurative Quranic use based on the color and visible extension of the whiteness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Kindling or inflammation of fire.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A nominal or verbal-noun expression for fire becoming inflamed or burning.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become spread or dispersed.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Attested of horsemen dispersing during a hostile or predatory raid.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To go far in an affair.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used with an affair as the object of the preposition فِي.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a horse, to have the white marking called شَعَلٌ or شُعْلَةٌ.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A descriptive use concerning a horse exhibiting the specified whiteness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To kindle a fire, making it burn brightly, fiercely, blaze, or flame.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used transitively with fire, especially fire in fuel or firewood; the intensive sense emphasizes vigorous burning.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To kindle or intensify war; to excite or inflame anger.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used figuratively with war or anger.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To smear camels extensively with tar.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized transitive use referring to broad application of tar rather than only to isolated sores or scabs.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To spread or disperse a group, or to become dispersed.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of horsemen, camels, a congregation, or a raid; the same lexical branch also occurs in an intransitive construction describing a raid whose participants disperse.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To discharge blood, water, or tears in a scattered or copious flow.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a wound emitting blood, a waterskin or water-bag shedding water, or an eye shedding abundant tears.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make irrigation water abundant.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized use with water supplied for irrigation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become kindled, burn brightly or fiercely, blaze, or flame.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used intransitively of fire, especially fire in fuel or firewood.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become excited or inflamed with anger; to become filled with wrath.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative intransitive use with anger or wrath understood as the accompanying state.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of hair, to become separated, loosened, ruffled, or bristling.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of the hair of the head becoming disordered or standing out.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A man who is light, agile, active, clever, ingenious, acute, or sharp.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An attributive description of a person combining quick movement with mental alertness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A white marking in a horse's tail, forelock, head, or related hair.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Reports differ on the precise location: it is chiefly associated with the tail, but may also denote whiteness in the forelock, head, or side of the tail.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A firebrand, a piece of wood in which fire is kindled, a lighted wick, or a flame.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The word covers a portable burning piece or flame; it is also used for the lighted or burnt extremity of a wick.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A party, division, sect, distinct body, or class of people.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A collective designation for a distinct group or division.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Glowing embers or fire-touched tinder, including material resembling stars at the bottom of a cooking pot.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of residual glowing material or a burnt rag into which fire has fallen.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A lighted wick or an oil- or grease-soaked wick containing fire.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The item is called this when it is actually kindled and used to give light.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Scattered or dispersed things or persons; to go away in a dispersed state.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A plural expression used of scattered portions, people, or groups that have dispersed.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who or that which kindles, or something possessing the quality of kindling.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The word may be analyzed as an active participle or as a possessive epithet meaning ‘possessing kindling’; its attested use is connected with something burning or causing vigorous burning.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A horse having a white marking of the type called شُعْلَةٌ or شَعَلٌ.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The feminine form is شَعْلَاءُ; the marking may include a blaze on the forehead extending over one eye.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A lamp of the kind called قِنْدِيلٌ.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A concrete lighting implement.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Kindled, burning brightly or fiercely, blazing, or flaming.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The passive-participial adjective is used of fire or a fire-like blaze.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Numerous and spreading in every direction; dispersed like a swarm of locusts.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of locusts and extended to an army or military force advancing in a spreading or dispersed formation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A skin vessel on four wooden legs, used as a trough-like container for preparing or holding nabīdh.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A desert implement, also called مِشْعَالٌ; its plural is مَشَاعِلُ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A clarifier or strainer for wine and similar liquids.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized technical sense of the same noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A large support or cresset for carrying a light or burning material.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: It may consist of a staff with one or more receptacles for flaming wood, tarred rags, or similar fuel, and may be carried before travelers at night.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An instrument or container in which fire is carried.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The vocalized form with kasrah on the initial mīm denotes the fire-bearing implement; it is closely related to the cresset sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Fire that has been kindled or made to burn brightly, fiercely, blaze, or flame.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The vocalized form with fatḥah on the initial mīm is used adjectivally or nominally for kindled fire.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A bearer of a cresset; by extension, a nightman, well-cleaner, scavenger, or executioner.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: These occupational senses develop from association with the cresset and its use in night work, well cleaning, removal of refuse, and execution.

The literal fire and anger meanings of اِشْتَعَلَ are broader Classical Arabic usages and are kept separate from the Quranic gray-hair sense.
